mainTopic: Minimum amounts (שיעורים) for carrying materials on שבת, the size of a קשר מוכסין, and whether a used tax receipt or a repaid שטר still counts as having value.
overview: This amud finishes the משנה's list of minimum amounts (שיעורים) for הוצאה, carrying from one domain to another on שבת. Each material is measured by the smallest useful thing people normally do with it, and רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה disagree about some items. The גמרא then explains why rope does not get reed's smaller measure: people do not use rope that way. A ברייתא adds more items, and the גמרא shows that the סלע and the dried-fig measures for fat are really the same amount. Next the גמרא asks how big a קשר מוכסין (tax receipt) is. רב ששת and רבא each explain it differently, and a ברייתא about erased paper leaves רבא with an unanswered קשיא. Two ברייתות then ask whether a used tax receipt or a repaid שטר חוב still has value, with רבי יהודה saying it does 'because he needs it.' אמוראים offer different explanations of the practical difference in each dispute. The amud ends by asking how אביי reads the ברייתא's 'before repaid' and 'after repaid', and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Measures for paper, hide, parchment and ink
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the minimum amounts for erased paper, hide, דוכסוסטוס, קלף and ink.
steps.simpleTranslation: Erased paper: enough to wrap a small perfume jar. Hide: enough to make an amulet. דוכסוסטוס: enough to write a מזוזה. קלף: enough to write the shortest section of the תפילין, which is שמע ישראל. Ink: enough to write two letters.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps listing items and tells us how much of each one you must carry on שבת to be liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each measure is tied to the smallest normal use of that material. Erased paper can no longer be written on, so its measure comes from wrapping. Writing materials are measured by the smallest meaningful piece of writing they could hold.

keyTerms.meaning: Paper whose writing has been erased
The inner layer of a split hide, used for a מזוזה
Parchment (the outer layer of the hide), used for תפילין

steps.confusionAlert: Each kind of hide gets the measure of what it is normally written on. Do not assume all parchment shares one measure. דוכסוסטוס is measured by a מזוזה, and קלף is measured by the smallest תפילין section.

phrases.english: Erased paper: enough to wrap
around a small jar of perfume.
Hide: enough to make an amulet.
Dokhsostos: enough to write a mezuza.
Parchment: enough to write on it
the smallest section in the tefillin,
which is 'Shema Yisrael'.
Ink: enough to write two letters.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְיָיר מָחוּק — כְּדֵי לִכְרוֹךְ עַל צְלוֹחִית קְטַנָּה שֶׁל פִּלְיָיטוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of שיעורים from the previous amud (78a).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liability for carrying writing materials depends on having enough for their smallest normal use.

steps.title: Measures for eye paint, glue, tar and wax
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives measures for כחול, glue, tar and sulfur, and wax.
steps.simpleTranslation: Eye paint: enough to paint one eye. Glue: enough to put on top of a bird-trapping stick. Tar and sulfur: enough to make a small hole. Wax: enough to plug the opening of a small hole.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves on from writing materials to cosmetics and sealing materials, giving each one a small practical measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here too the measure follows real-life use. The measure is only one eye. The גמרא later asks about this, since people do not usually paint just one eye. Tar and sulfur are measured by sealing a crack and leaving a tiny hole in the seal.

keyTerms.meaning: Blue eye paint, like kohl or eye shadow
A stick or board smeared with glue to catch birds

phrases.english: Blue eye paint: enough to paint one eye.
Glue: enough to put on the top of the bird-trap stick.
Tar and sulfur: enough to make a hole.

phrases.aramaic: שַׁעֲוָה — כְּדֵי לִיתֵּן עַל פִּי נֶקֶב קָטָן.
phrases.english: Wax: enough to put on the opening of a small hole.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list with new categories of materials.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cosmetic and sealing materials are measured by their smallest practical use.

steps.title: Measures for crushed earthenware and bran
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives the measure for חרסית, רבי יהודה offers a different one, and then the משנה gives the measure for bran.
steps.simpleTranslation: Crushed earthenware: enough to make the opening of a goldsmiths' furnace. רבי יהודה says: enough to make a small stand. Bran: enough to put on the opening of a goldsmiths' furnace.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists materials that goldsmiths use. רבי יהודה disagrees about the measure for crushed earthenware.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא measures חרסית by the opening where the bellows connects to the furnace. רבי יהודה measures it by a small stand, which is a different minimum use. Bran is measured by being placed at the furnace opening.

keyTerms.meaning: A small tripod or stand for the crucible

phrases.english: Crushed earthenware: enough to make
the opening of a gold refiners' crucible.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: כְּדֵי לַעֲשׂוֹת פִּיטְפּוּט.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: enough to make a small tripod.
Bran: enough to put

phrases.aramaic: עַל פִּי כוּר שֶׁל צוֹרְפֵי זָהָב.
phrases.english: on the opening of a gold refiners' crucible.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַרְסִית — כְּדֵי לַעֲשׂוֹת פִּי כוּר שֶׁל צוֹרְפֵי זָהָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list and introduces a disagreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The measure for חרסית is disputed: the opening of a furnace (תנא קמא) or a small stand (רבי יהודה).

steps.title: Measure for lime, a three-way disagreement
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives the measure for lime, and רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה each give a different one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Lime: enough to smear on the smallest of girls. רבי יהודה says: enough to smooth down the hair at the temple. רבי נחמיה says: enough to smear on the temple to remove fine hairs.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends its list with lime. Three opinions appear, each based on a different cosmetic use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא measures lime by its use as a hair remover on a young girl's small body. רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה each tie it to a different use on the temple area. The amount needed differs with each use.

keyTerms.meaning: Lime, used here as a hair remover
Hair growing at the temple, or smoothing that hair down
The temple area, or the fine hairs there

steps.whatToRemember: Every שיעור in the משנה follows one principle: you are liable only when you carry an amount that people normally consider useful for that material.

phrases.english: Lime: enough to smear on the smallest of the girls.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: כְּדֵי לַעֲשׂוֹת כִּלְכּוּל.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: enough to smooth the hair of the temple.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה אוֹמֵר: כְּדֵי לָסוּד אוּנְדִּפֵי.
phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya says: enough to smear on the temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The measure for lime is disputed among the תנא קמא, רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה.

steps.title: Why doesn't rope have the smaller measure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why rope should not make you liable at the smaller measure of a hanging loop for a sieve, the measure given for reed.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Rope should also make one liable at the amount needed to make a hanging loop for a sifter or a sieve!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by challenging the measure the משנה gave for rope.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה measured rope by a basket handle, but measured reed by a smaller hanging loop for a sieve. Rope could make that loop too, so the smaller measure should apply to rope as well.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rope too, let one be liable
for enough to make a loop for hanging a sifter and a sieve!

steps.triggerLanguage: חֶבֶל נָמֵי לִיחַיֵּיב כְּדֵי לַעֲשׂוֹת תְּלַאי לַנָּפָה וְלַכְּבָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא and goes back to the rope measure from the משנה on the previous amud (78a).
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's measure for rope, which is the size of a basket handle
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rope can do everything reed can, so it should share reed's smaller measure.

steps.title: Rope damages the sieve
steps.stepSummary: Rope is rough and cuts grooves into the sieve, so people do not use it for hanging loops.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it cuts grooves into the vessel, people do not do this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that rope is not normally used to hang a sieve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A measure depends on what people actually do, not on what is technically possible. Rope would wear grooves into the wooden frame, so nobody uses it that way. That use therefore does not set its measure.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a basic rule of הוצאה measures: they follow normal human practice.

phrases.english: Since it cuts grooves into the vessel,
people do not do so.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּחָרֵיק בְּמָנָא לָא עָבְדִי אִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical distinction based on normal use
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Rope should share reed's smaller measure.
steps.terutzMaskana: Rope is not normally used for sieve loops, so the basket-handle measure stands.

steps.title: A ברייתא adds palm leaves, bast and fat
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives measures for palm leaves, bast (according to אחרים) and fat, and says fat is the size of a סלע.
steps.simpleTranslation: תנו רבנן: Palm leaves: enough to make a handle for an Egyptian basket. Bast: אחרים say enough to put on the opening of a small funnel to strain wine. Fat: enough to grease under a small cake. How much is that? The size of a סלע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds more items and their measures to the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These items are not in our משנה, so the ברייתא fills in the gaps using the same 'smallest normal use' approach. For fat it also gives a concrete size, the size of a סלע coin.

keyTerms.meaning: Bast, the fibrous material from palm trees
A coin of a known size

phrases.english: The Sages taught: Palm leaves: enough to make
a handle for an Egyptian wicker basket.
Bast: Others say:

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי לִיתֵּן עַל פִּי מַשְׁפֵּךְ קָטָן
phrases.english: enough to put on the opening of a small funnel
to filter the wine.
Fat: enough to smear
beneath a small cake.
And how much is its measure? Like a sela.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הוּצִין כְּדֵי לַעֲשׂוֹת אוֹזֶן לְסַל כְּפִיפָה מִצְרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section that adds to the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fat is measured by greasing under a small cake, which is the size of a סלע.

steps.title: Another ברייתא says the size of a dried fig
steps.stepSummary: A different ברייתא gives the measure of fat as the size of a dried fig, not a סלע.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: the size of a dried fig!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that a different ברייתא gives a different measure for fat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One source says the size of a סלע and another says the size of a גרוגרת. At first glance these look like two different amounts, so the sources seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: A dried fig, a standard measure

phrases.english: But it was taught: like a dried fig!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the measure of fat given in step 7.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two ברייתות seem to give different amounts for the same item.

steps.title: Both are the same amount
steps.stepSummary: The סלע and the dried fig are really the same measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one and that one are one measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is no real contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An amount of fat equal to a dried fig, when spread out, covers the area of a סלע coin. One ברייתא describes the area and the other describes the amount, but both mean the same thing.

phrases.english: This and that are one measure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Harmonization: the same measure described in two ways
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות disagree about the measure of fat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The סלע area and the גרוגרת amount describe the same quantity.

steps.title: Measure for soft stuffing material
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: soft material is measured by a small ball, which is the size of a nut.
steps.simpleTranslation: Soft material: enough to make a small ball. How much is that? The size of a nut.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא with one more item and its size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again the ברייתא names the normal use, a small ball, and then turns it into a known size, a nut. This makes the measure easy to apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Soft material, such as wool scraps or stuffing

phrases.english: Soft material: enough to make a small ball,
and how much is its measure? Like a nut.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The measure for מוכין is a small ball, the size of a nut.

steps.title: How big is a קשר מוכסין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that paper is measured by a tax receipt, and a תנא explains this means space for two tax-receipt letters.
steps.simpleTranslation: Paper: enough to write a tax receipt on it. A תנא taught: How big is a tax receipt? Two letters of a tax receipt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה's measure for paper and brings a source that defines its size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא explains that a קשר מוכסין only needs two letters. These are the special large letters that tax collectors used. This sets up the contradiction that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: A tax receipt, a small note from the tax collector

phrases.aramaic: נְיָיר — כְּדֵי לִכְתּוֹב עָלָיו קֶשֶׁר מוֹכְסִין.
phrases.english: Paper: enough to write a tax receipt on it.
A tanna taught: How much is a tax receipt?
Two letters of a tax receipt.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְיָיר — כְּדֵי לִכְתּוֹב עָלָיו קֶשֶׁר מוֹכְסִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the paper measure from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The paper measure is two tax-receipt letters, which are larger than ordinary letters.

steps.title: Blank paper requires only two letters
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says carrying blank paper makes one liable if it has room for just two letters, which seems smaller than a tax receipt.
steps.simpleTranslation: They contrasted it: One who carries out blank paper, if it has room to write two letters, is liable. If not, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction to the tax-receipt measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא speaks of two ordinary letters, while the tax receipt needs two large letters. So the blank-paper ברייתא seems to require less paper than our sources do.

keyTerms.meaning: And they contrasted it; this introduces a contradicting source

phrases.english: And they contrasted: One who carries out blank paper,

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ בּוֹ כְּדֵי לִכְתּוֹב שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת — חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: if it has enough to write two letters, he is liable,
and if not, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the measure defined in step 11.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two ordinary letters take less space than two tax-receipt letters, so the sources disagree.

steps.title: רב ששת: these are tax-receipt letters too
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the 'two letters' of the blank-paper ברייתא are also large tax-receipt letters.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: What are 'two letters'? Two letters of a tax receipt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת resolves the contradiction by reading the blank-paper ברייתא differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He says that when the ברייתא wrote 'two letters', it meant the large letters of a tax receipt. So both sources require the same, larger amount of paper.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: מַאי שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת?
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: What are 'two letters'?
Two letters of a tax receipt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: מַאי שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction in step 12.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Two letters' means large tax-receipt letters, so the sources agree.

steps.title: רבא: two ordinary letters plus a margin
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that a tax receipt equals two ordinary letters plus a blank margin to hold the paper.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Two of our letters plus a space to hold it, and that equals a tax receipt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second way to resolve the contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not say the letters are large. He says a קשר מוכסין is two ordinary letters plus a margin to hold the note by. Since any written paper needs such a margin, the blank-paper ברייתא matches that same size.

keyTerms.meaning: A margin or place to hold the paper

steps.whatToRemember: Both אמוראים agree that the paper measure equals a tax receipt. They disagree only about why: רב ששת says the letters are large, and רבא says ordinary letters plus a holding margin.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not reject the tax-receipt measure. He explains that a tax receipt is the size of two ordinary letters plus a margin.

phrases.english: Rava said: Two letters of ours
and a place to hold it,
which is the size of a tax receipt.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת דִּידַן וּבֵית אֲחִיזָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from רב ששת's to the same contradiction.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Tax-receipt letters must be larger than ordinary letters.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two ordinary letters plus a holding margin equal a קשר מוכסין, so both sources agree.

steps.title: A ברייתא on erased paper and repaid documents is quoted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: carrying erased paper or a repaid שטר makes one liable if its blank area can hold two letters, or if the whole sheet can wrap a small perfume flask.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: Someone who carries out erased paper or a repaid loan document is liable if its blank part has room to write two letters, or if the whole thing is big enough to wrap around the top of a small perfume flask. If not, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא in order to challenge one of the earlier answers. This step only sets up the source. The actual attack comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives the measure for blank, useless paper as room for 'two letters.' The next step checks whether this fits רב ששת and רבא from steps 13–14.

keyTerms.meaning: A loan document whose debt was already paid
The white, blank part of the paper

phrases.english: They challenged: One who carries out erased paper
or a repaid loan document,
if there is in its blank part
enough room to write two letters,
or the whole of it is enough to wrap

phrases.aramaic: עַל פִּי צְלוֹחִית קְטַנָּה שֶׁל פִּלְיָיטוֹן —
phrases.english: around the mouth of a small perfume flask —
he is liable; and if not — he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source to test the explanations of רב ששת and רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's explanation that a tax receipt equals two ordinary letters plus a margin for holding
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This step sets up the source. The attack itself is spelled out in step 16.

steps.title: The ברייתא fits רב ששת but not רבא, and the challenge stands
steps.stepSummary: For רב ששת, 'two letters' means tax-receipt letters, so the ברייתא fits. For רבא, the tax-receipt size includes a margin for holding. Erased paper doesn't need such a margin, yet the ברייתא doesn't make the measure smaller. The challenge is left unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for רב ששת, who said 'two letters' means two tax-receipt letters. But for רבא, who said a tax receipt is two of our letters plus a space to hold it, here no holding space is needed! It is a difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the ברייתא fits רב ששת but contradicts רבא. It ends with 'קשיא,' meaning the problem is left unsolved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא explained that the extra size of a tax receipt is a blank margin for holding the paper. Erased or repaid paper can be held anywhere, so under רבא its measure should be smaller. Since the ברייתא still uses the same 'two letters,' רבא's explanation is challenged and no answer is given.

keyTerms.meaning: A blank margin for holding the paper

steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' at the end does not mean רבא is fully rejected like 'תיובתא.' It means the difficulty remains without an answer.

phrases.english: It works well for Rav Sheshet, who said
what is meant by 'two letters,'

phrases.aramaic: שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת שֶׁל קֶשֶׁר מוֹכְסִין — שַׁפִּיר.
phrases.english: two letters of a tax receipt — it is fine.
But according to Rava, who said
two of our letters plus a space for holding,
which is the size of a tax receipt —
here a space for holding is not needed!
It is a difficulty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the quoted ברייתא against רבא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבא, the holding margin is part of the measure. Erased paper needs no margin, so its measure should be smaller, but the ברייתא keeps it the same.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The challenge against רבא stays unresolved. רב ששת's explanation fits the ברייתא.
steps.whatToRemember: The blank-paper ברייתא supports רב ששת and leaves רבא with an unanswered קשיא.

steps.title: Carrying a tax receipt before or after showing it
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: carrying a tax receipt before showing it to the collector makes one liable, and after showing it one is exempt. רבי יהודה says one is liable even after, because he still needs it.
steps.simpleTranslation: תנו רבנן: One who carries out a tax receipt before showing it to the tax collector is liable. After showing it, he is exempt. רבי יהודה says: Even after showing it he is liable, because he still needs it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about when a tax receipt still counts as an item worth carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, one is liable only for carrying something that has value. The ת״ק holds that once the receipt was shown, it is useless. רבי יהודה holds it still has a use.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: One who carries out a tax receipt,
before he showed it to the tax collector — is liable.
Once he showed it to the tax collector — he is exempt.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Even once he showed it to the tax collector he is liable
because he needs it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the size of a tax receipt to whether it still has value after use.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ת״ק: exempt after showing it. רבי יהודה: liable even after, since he still needs it.

steps.title: What is the practical difference in the tax-receipt dispute?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in what real situation the ת״ק and רבי יהודה would rule differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what real case the dispute is about. This sets up three answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a receipt is useless once shown, so the גמרא wants to know when רבי יהודה would still think it is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the dispute just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical case where the ת״ק and רבי יהודה disagree.

steps.title: אביי: Tax inspectors who chase after travelers
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the difference is about tax runners, inspectors who check people after they already passed the collector.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The difference between them is the tax runners.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the first answer. Sometimes inspectors run after people to check that they paid, so the receipt might be needed again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where such inspectors exist, רבי יהודה says the receipt still has value. The ת״ק ignores this possibility and treats the receipt as used up.

keyTerms.meaning: Tax runners (inspectors who check after the collector)
There is a difference between them

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The difference between them is the tax runners.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case of follow-up inspectors (tax runners).

steps.title: רבא: A junior and a senior tax collector
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the difference is when there is a junior collector and then a senior one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The difference between them is a senior tax collector and a junior tax collector.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second answer. After passing a junior collector, a person may still need to show the receipt to a senior one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's case is a second official checkpoint, not inspectors running after people. In that case רבי יהודה holds the receipt still has value.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹכֵס גָּדוֹל וּמוֹכֵס קָטָן אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ.
phrases.english: A senior tax collector and a junior tax collector — that is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: מוֹכֵס גָּדוֹל וּמוֹכֵס קָטָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer from אביי's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case of two levels of tax officials.

steps.title: רב אשי: Even with one collector, the receipt proves he is trusted
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says they disagree even with only one collector, because the receipt can be shown to a future collector as proof of good standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: They differ even with one tax collector, because he needs to show it to a second collector, saying: 'Look, I am a man of the tax collector.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a third answer. Even with no second checkpoint on this trip, the old receipt helps later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב אשי, the receipt's value is not as proof of payment. It is a kind of reference letter showing the person is on good terms with the tax authorities. רבי יהודה counts that as a real use.

keyTerms.meaning: A man connected to (trusted by) the tax collector

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Even one tax collector is a difference between them,

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לוֹ לְהַרְאוֹת לְמוֹכֵס שֵׁנִי,
phrases.english: because he needs it to show to a second tax collector,
since he says to him: Look,
I am a man of the tax collector.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: חַד מוֹכֵס אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer, broader than the first two.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even with one collector, since the receipt shows good standing to future collectors.
steps.whatToRemember: Three explanations of רבי יהודה's 'he still needs it': אביי says inspectors, רבא says a senior collector, and רב אשי says proof of good standing for the future.

steps.title: Carrying a loan document before or after repayment
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: carrying a שטר חוב before repayment makes one liable, and after repayment one is exempt. רבי יהודה says one is liable even after, because he needs it.
steps.simpleTranslation: תנו רבנן: One who carries out a loan document before it was repaid is liable. Once repaid, he is exempt. רבי יהודה says: Even once repaid he is liable, because he needs it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא with the same pattern as the tax-receipt ברייתא, this time about a loan document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is again whether a 'used up' document still has value. This links back to the 'שטר פרוע' mentioned in step 15.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: One who carries out a loan document,
before it was repaid — is liable;
once it was repaid — he is exempt.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Even once it was repaid — he is liable,
because he needs it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ברייתא to the tax-receipt case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ת״ק: exempt after repayment. רבי יהודה: liable even after repayment.

steps.title: What is the practical difference in the loan-document dispute?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ת״ק and רבי יהודה really disagree about here.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind this dispute. This sets up two answers, from רב יוסף and from אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a loan is paid, the document seems pointless. The גמרא wants to know why רבי יהודה still sees value in it.

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying issue in the loan-document dispute.

steps.title: רב יוסף: Whether one may keep a repaid document
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says רבנן forbid keeping a repaid שטר, so it is worthless. רבי יהודה permits keeping it, so it has value.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: The difference is whether it is forbidden to keep a repaid document. רבנן hold it is forbidden to keep a repaid document. רבי יהודה holds it is permitted to keep a repaid document.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains that the ברייתא's dispute depends on a monetary-law question: may a repaid loan document be kept?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If keeping a repaid שטר is forbidden (so the lender can't collect twice), it must be destroyed and has no value, so carrying it is exempt. If keeping it is permitted, it can be used, for example as paper, so it has value and carrying it brings liability.

keyTerms.meaning: It is forbidden to keep (hold on to)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: אָסוּר לְשַׁהוֹת שְׁטָר פָּרוּעַ אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ.
phrases.english: Whether it is forbidden to keep a repaid document is the difference between them.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: אָסוּר לְשַׁהוֹת שְׁטָר פָּרוּעַ.
phrases.english: The Rabbis hold: It is forbidden to keep a repaid document.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: מוּתָּר לְשַׁהוֹת שְׁטָר פָּרוּעַ.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda holds: It is permitted to keep a repaid document.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: אָסוּר לְשַׁהוֹת שְׁטָר פָּרוּעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is whether one may keep a repaid שטר.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a שבת liability can depend on a monetary-law (חושן משפט) rule. Whether an item is 'valuable' depends on whether one may legally keep it.

steps.title: אביי: The dispute is about confirming a document the borrower admits writing
steps.stepSummary: אביי says everyone forbids keeping a repaid שטר. The real dispute is whether a document the borrower admits writing still needs court confirmation (קיום).
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Everyone agrees it is forbidden to keep a repaid document. Here they argue about a borrower who admits he wrote the document, and whether it still needs to be confirmed in court. The ת״ק holds it needs confirmation. רבי יהודה holds it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects רב יוסף's reason and offers a different underlying dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, the argument is about whether a borrower's admission that he wrote the שטר is enough, or whether the lender still needs the court to confirm the signatures (קיום השטר). How this connects to 'before repaid' and 'after repaid' in the ברייתא is not yet clear, which leads to the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: A borrower who admits he wrote the document
To confirm it (validate its signatures in court)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two answers. רב יוסף says the dispute is about keeping a paid שטר. אביי says everyone forbids that, and the dispute is about court confirmation of a שטר the borrower admits writing.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אָסוּר לְשַׁהוֹת שְׁטָר פָּרוּעַ,
phrases.english: Everyone agrees it is forbidden to keep a repaid document,
and here, about one who admits a document that he wrote,
whether it needs to be confirmed — they disagree:

phrases.aramaic: תַּנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר מוֹדֶה בִּשְׁטָר שֶׁכְּתָבוֹ —
phrases.english: The first Tanna holds: one who admits a document that he wrote —
it needs to be confirmed.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר מוֹדֶה בִּשְׁטָר שֶׁכְּתָבוֹ —
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda holds: one who admits a document that he wrote —
it does not need to be confirmed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אֲמַר: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אָסוּר לְשַׁהוֹת שְׁטָר פָּרוּעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב יוסף's explanation and offers another.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is about whether an admitted שטר needs court confirmation (קיום).

steps.title: How does אביי read 'before repaid' and 'after repaid'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא's words 'before he repaid' and 'once he repaid' mean under אביי's explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is meant by 'before he repaid it' and 'once he repaid it'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how אביי's explanation fits the wording of the ברייתא. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי moved the dispute to court confirmation, but the ברייתא clearly talks about before and after repayment. The גמרא now needs to show how that wording fits אביי's view.

phrases.english: And what is meant by 'before he repaid it'
and 'once he repaid it'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests אביי's explanation against the ברייתא's wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the ברייתא's 'before/after repayment' wording fits אביי's explanation about court confirmation.
